title: e1.12 — reviewing a 500-commit agent repository entirely inside fathom's TUI
comment: The acceptance script of reco-glv, as data. `python3 tools/tui_session.py --root <fixture> \
The reviewer here did not write any of the code under review and never touches the mouse.
The fixture is `python3 tools/agent_fixture.py --out /tmp/harbour-mvp` (500 commits, 213 turns,
3 agents and 2 humans) indexed with `fathom index`. `shell` steps run between keystrokes: those
are the things that genuinely happen in another terminal, like the rebase in part D.

steps.note: A: open `fathom tui` on an indexed repository — 500 commits, epoch 1 ready (part A: orient). The queue is the landing view, and it has no episodes in it
the keymap overlay: the three canonical tasks, every action with its key. A newcomer can read the whole contract without leaving the TUI
close the help
the timeline — the reviewer's front page. The rail is where 213 agent turns should be listed
walk the rail with j/k: the cursor has nowhere to go, because the shell hands the rail no episodes at all
jump to first row
jump to last row
the filter form: author, kind, state, area, date range, path fragment — nine composable filters, all of them functional, none of them with anything to filter
<C-n>/<C-p> move the form, <Enter> chooses. Keyboard-only so far, exactly as ADR-006 §9 promises
close the filters
the attention queue: what should a human look at first. Nothing is ranked, because nothing is loaded
the command palette: every action in the registry is reachable from here, which is the keyboard-reachability promise (K1)
type to narrow: 'Jump to first unread episode' is a real, bound action
run it. With no episodes loaded, 'first unread' is silent — no count, no empty-state sentence
B: find the riskiest episodes (part B). Search is the reviewer's other front door: free text plus author:/path:/risk>/dep: tokens
search for the planted one: a production Stripe key added to CI, three lines long — the change a size-ranked list hides
submit. The search view closes and the toast says the scorer belongs to e5.2: no match count, no empty state, no landing spot
n/N walk the matches. With no scorer there are no matches and the key is silent
second of the three riskiest: a migration that drops a column with no rollback file
search the SQL itself
same answer
the diff viewer (part B, reading). e1.8's materialiser and the diff viewer's eighteen golden fixtures are real; nothing in the shell ever hands them a patch
hunk motion, then i (intent), w (why this risk), x (mark reviewed): four keys over an empty scope. Each one is the review loop the product is for
intent, then the risk explanation, on the episode in scope — which is no episode
mark reviewed: the acceptance criterion (d) is 'a rebase must not lose this'. It cannot be set, so it cannot be checked
endpoint mark for compare-with-mark; the toast is honest about e5.3 owning the comparison
the artefact view: the review record you would post on the PR
ambient mode: the second-terminal glance
structure view
graph view — `g` is also the first key of `gg`, so the frame marks the 250 ms wait before it opens (`reco-wlt`)
deps view
zoom the focused pane; <C-w>h/l move focus, T pins a tab — the frame's own motions all work
D: the rebase (part D) starts here. First, re-index from inside the TUI after the history moves — the shell has no store handle, so this key can only narrate

steps.shell: tip=$(git rev-parse HEAD); base=$(git rev-parse HEAD~5); git reset --hard -q $base && git cherry-pick $(git rev-list --reverse $base..$tip) >/dev/null && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc -q --prune=now; echo "head=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) commits=$(git rev-list --all --count)"
steps.note: another terminal rewrites the last five commits — the force-push case ADR-003 exists for. The five old commits are unreachable: pruned, not hidden
the open TUI notices none of it: the watcher is a separate verb and no producer feeds the frame
so the reviewer asks the shell to re-index, and the shell says it has no store handle and names e1.4, a ticket that closed weeks ago
the index catches up in a separate process: 5 rewalked, 0 new — the rewritten commits are the same content, and the identity digest is what makes that true
quit. e1.11 writes the session on the way out: the filter, the pinned tab, the layout, the `m` mark, the last search
from another terminal, with the TUI shut: what the repository remembers about the reviewer after a rewritten history — this is the review state the build can hold
reopen: the toast names what came back, and `t` is the timeline again on the rewritten history — same rail, same message telling the reviewer to run an index that is already done
end of the walkthrough: no mouse, no leaving the TUI except where the work genuinely is elsewhere, and no episode ever read
